match_nodes.description: Stop Hacks and Improve Electronic Data Security Act

data.official_name: Stop Hacks and Improve Electronic Data Security Act
data.description: Broad-scope data breach notification and security requirements. Effective 2020.
data.notes: Broadened the definition of private information and expanded breach notification requirements beyond New York residents. Requires businesses that collect private information of New York residents to implement reasonable safeguards: administrative (designate coordinator, train employees), technical (assess risks, detect attacks), and physical (detect/prevent intrusions, dispose data securely). Applies to any person or business that owns or licenses computerized data including private information of a New York resident, regardless of where the business is located.

match_nodes.description: NYC Local Law 144 (Automated Employment Decision Tools)

data.description: New York City law regulating the use of automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) in hiring and promotion.
data.notes: Effective July 5, 2023. Requires employers using AEDTs to: conduct annual independent bias audits, publish audit results, notify candidates of AEDT use, and allow candidates to request alternative selection processes. Enforced by NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP). Penalties range from $500 to $1,500 per violation. First US law specifically regulating AI in hiring decisions.

data.official_name: New York General Business Law Article 47 (§§ 1700–1704) — Artificial Intelligence Companion Models
data.common_name: NY AI Companion Models Law (GBL Art. 47)
alternate_names: S3008-C / A3008-C Part U (FY 2026 Enacted Budget)
data.description: New York state statute requiring operators of AI companion models to provide clear and conspicuous notice at the start of every interaction and at least every three hours during continuing interactions that the user is not communicating with a human, and to maintain suicidal-ideation and self-harm detection and crisis-service referral protocols.
data.notes: Status: In force November 5, 2025 (enacted May 9, 2025 as Part U of the FY 2026 Transportation, Economic Development and Environmental Conservation Budget Bill, S3008-C / A3008-C, effective 180 days after enactment; verified as of 2026-11-03). Enforced by the New York Attorney General with civil penalties up to $15,000 per day directed to the New York State Suicide Prevention Fund.
